name: Software Engineering

topics.why: 27 questions, 14 papers; matching and classification dominate.
Frequent (23 of 144, 13 papers) with agile/cleanroom/ordering variants every few papers.
what_to_study: Agile model list, principles, FDD order

topics.why: 22 questions in 11 papers; SRS attributes, UML and elicitation repeat.
what_to_study: UML diagram types and purpose, sequence diagrams
Cohesion and coupling ranking and definitions

topics.why: 7 questions but in 6 of 15 papers (40%); small but recurring.

clusters.title: Agile: which models/principles are agile
clusters.technique: Agile = XP, Scrum, FDD, ASD, Crystal, DSDM; NOT waterfall/spiral/incremental. Agile principles favour change, customer collaboration, working software, delivering increments; 'following the plan' is the anti-principle.
clusters.what_changes: Pick-the-agile-models, odd-one-out principle, or correct handling of unpredictability
clusters.skip_note: All three test 'agile = embrace change, incremental delivery'; one pass covers all.

clusters.title: Agile/FDD sequence and artifact matching
clusters.technique: Memorise FDD order: overall model, feature list, plan by feature, design by feature, build by feature. Agile flow: plan, design, develop, test, release. Scrum=sprint backlog, XP=CRC cards, ASD=speculate-collaborate-learn.
clusters.what_changes: Ordering vs matching of agile phases/artifacts
clusters.skip_note: Same memorised sequences/artifacts reappear; learn the lists once.

clusters.title: Cleanroom software engineering
clusters.technique: Cleanroom: incremental model, formal specification, statistical (usage-based) testing and certification, correctness verification (static); no unit testing/dynamic verification by developers.
clusters.what_changes: Which statement is false / which is not a strategy
clusters.skip_note: Same 3-4 facts about cleanroom each time.

clusters.title: Process model suitability matching
clusters.technique: Waterfall=stable requirements; incremental=core product quickly; evolutionary/prototype=unclear reqs; component-based=reuse, compromises inevitable; spiral=risk driven.
clusters.skip_note: Both are the same model-to-situation table.

clusters.title: Spiral model characteristics
clusters.technique: Spiral = risk-driven, evolutionary/cyclic, suited to changing/unclear requirements, large projects.

clusters.title: Prototype model phase order
clusters.technique: Order: requirements/quick play -> quick design -> build prototype -> customer evaluation -> refine -> deliver/engineer final product.
clusters.what_changes: Wording of steps differs, order same

clusters.title: SRS quality attribute definitions
clusters.technique: Map definition to attribute: unambiguous=one interpretation, consistent=no conflicts, verifiable=cost-effective check, complete, modifiable, traceable, ranked. Reliability is not an SRS attribute.
clusters.what_changes: Which attribute / which is NOT an attribute
clusters.skip_note: Same attribute list, different definition asked.

clusters.title: Elicitation and validation techniques
clusters.technique: Elicitation: interviews, questionnaires, ethnography (observation), prototyping, use cases/scenarios, JAD; DFD is analysis, not elicitation. Inspection/reviews/prototype/test-case generation validate requirements.
clusters.what_changes: Name the technique from its description

clusters.title: UML diagram identity and purpose
clusters.technique: Static/structural: class, object, component, deployment, use-case(static view per UGC key). Behavioural: state, activity, sequence, collaboration. Use-case = external actors interacting with system.
clusters.what_changes: Static vs dynamic, match diagram to description

clusters.title: Sequence diagram reading
clusters.technique: Count lifelines/objects and follow messages top to bottom in time order.
clusters.skip_note: Both from Dec 2019; read diagram carefully, no theory.

clusters.title: OO analysis/behaviour modelling step order
clusters.technique: OOA order: use-case + activity -> interaction (sequence) -> class -> state chart/object -> component/deployment. Behaviour model: evaluate use-cases, identify events, build state transition diagram, review.
clusters.skip_note: Both ask the ordered modelling steps.

clusters.title: Cohesion types and ranking
clusters.technique: Best to worst: functional > sequential > communicational > procedural > temporal > logical > coincidental. Communicational = same input/output data.

clusters.title: Coupling types
clusters.technique: Low to high: data < stamp < control < external < common < content. Common = shared global data; control = one module controls flow of another.
clusters.skip_note: One ranking plus definitions answers all.

clusters.title: Software engineering terms matching (coupling/cohesion=design)
clusters.technique: Product complexity-> metrics; structured analysis -> requirements; coupling & cohesion -> design; symbolic execution -> validation.
clusters.what_changes: Identical items, only the list-ordering differs

clusters.title: Design principle definitions matching
clusters.technique: Cohesion=intra-module strength, coupling=inter-module dependency, modularity=division, abstraction=hide details, encapsulation=packaging.
clusters.what_changes: Different terms in the match list

clusters.title: MVC component roles
clusters.technique: Model=business logic/domain data, View=UI presentation, Controller=handles input and updates model.

clusters.title: Productivity/effort/time arithmetic
clusters.technique: Effort = size/productivity; size = effort*productivity-rate; duration = effort/(team*hours per day).
clusters.skip_note: Same division; three came from one paper.

clusters.title: Cyclomatic complexity and flow graphs
clusters.technique: V(G)=E-N+2=P+1=number of regions; independent paths = V(G).
clusters.what_changes: Graph given, compute V(G) or related counts
clusters.skip_note: Single formula; the Dec 2019 passage gives five questions from one graph.

clusters.title: Availability from MTBF/downtime
clusters.technique: Availability = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR) = uptime fraction; downtime = (1-A)*period.
clusters.what_changes: Solve for repair time or availability

clusters.title: Software metric categories
clusters.technique: Size and complexity = product metrics; LOC/FP normalise by size (size-oriented); indirect measures = functionality, quality, reliability, maintainability.
clusters.skip_note: All from Sep 2022; one definition set.

clusters.title: COCOMO basics
clusters.technique: COCOMO = Constructive Cost Model; basic organic E=2.4(KLOC)^1.05 PM, D=2.5E^0.38; semidetached 3.0/1.12; embedded 3.6/1.20.

clusters.title: Types of maintenance
clusters.technique: Corrective=fix bugs, adaptive=new environment/platform, perfective=new features/restructuring for improvement, preventive=future maintainability.

clusters.title: Reengineering and reverse engineering
clusters.technique: Reverse engineering = recover design/spec from code (analysis only, no change); reengineering = reverse + forward restructuring; reasons: adapt, new tech, maintainability.

clusters.title: CMM maturity levels
clusters.technique: 1 Initial, 2 Repeatable (project mgmt), 3 Defined (process definition), 4 Managed (measurement), 5 Optimizing (continuous improvement).

clusters.title: Quality model attributes (ISO 9126)
clusters.technique: ISO 9126: functionality, reliability, usability, efficiency, maintainability, portability.

clusters.title: Configuration management and version control
clusters.technique: Commit source and documentation, not generated output; SCM provides versioning, branching, diff; Git is distributed VCS.

clusters.title: Quality control vs quality assurance
clusters.technique: QC = inspections/tests on products (detective); QA = process, preventive, no code execution.

clusters.title: Testing type matching
clusters.technique: Unit=component, integration=interfaces, system=whole, acceptance=user; regression=no new bugs; white box=condition coverage, black box=ECP/BVA.

clusters.title: Alpha and beta testing
clusters.technique: Alpha at developer site, beta at customer site; both acceptance testing.

clusters.title: Black-box vs white-box technique classification
clusters.technique: Black box: ECP, BVA, graph-based; white box: path, loop, data-flow, condition coverage.

clusters.title: Coverage criteria relations
clusters.technique: Path coverage subsumes branch and statement coverage; branch subsumes statement.
clusters.what_changes: Coverage test input or statement truth

clusters.title: Testing fundamentals statements
clusters.technique: Exhaustive testing impractical; testing effort needs early planning and is costly.

clusters.title: Verification vs validation
clusters.technique: Verification = built right (QA, reviews); validation = right product (user needs).

clusters.title: Risk management basics
clusters.technique: RE=P*L; risk categories project/technical/business; known/predictable/unpredictable; monitoring tracks if risks occur.

clusters.title: PERT/CPM and activity charts
clusters.technique: CPM repetitive jobs, PERT non-repetitive; critical path = longest path of dependent tasks defining duration; optimistic = shortest time.

examiner_mindset: Roughly 40% of questions are pure recall of definitions/lists; the rest are matching, ordering and true/false statement formats.
Favourite formats: Match List I/II and Arrange-in-order (CMM, prototype, agile, FDD, cohesion/coupling); expect one or two per paper.
Exact repeats are common: coupling statements (2018 x2), SE terms match (2018 and Dec 2022), prototype sequence, CMM order and match.
Numerics are few but reliable: 1-3 per paper (effort/productivity, cyclomatic, availability, reliability); numbers are rarely reused but formulas are.
Dec 2019 gave a five-question passage on a single flow graph; one unit can be a passage worth five marks.
Distractors: reorderings of the same list, 'All of the above/None' options, and a non-member (reliability for SRS, data flow diagram for elicitation, dynamic verification for cleanroom).
June 2024 Re-Exam leaned on easy arithmetic and definitions; Dec 2024 and June 2025 returned to ordering and 'A, B & D only' combos.
Cross-unit overlap: reliability/availability and verification vs validation touch Unit 2-style reliability; V&V appears under requirements and quality too.
He rarely asks deep COCOMO II/function point computation, EVM calculations beyond CPI, or code-level design patterns beyond proxy/MVC.
Topic tags are fuzzy: the same theme (maintenance, reengineering, V&V) is tagged under several topics, so study by theme.

formulas.name: Cyclomatic complexity
formulas.formula: V(G) = E - N + 2 = P + 1 = number of regions
formulas.note: P = predicate (decision) nodes; V(G) = number of independent paths

formulas.name: Cost performance index
formulas.note: Earned value over actual cost; schedule index SPI = BCWP/BCWS

formulas.name: Availability
formulas.note: Downtime = (1-A) x period; convert minutes/seconds carefully

formulas.name: Exponential reliability
formulas.formula: R(t) = e^(-t/MTTF), MTTF = mean of times between failures

formulas.name: Web app integrity
formulas.note: threat=probability of attack, security=probability of repelling

formulas.name: Software maturity index
formulas.note: Mt=modules in current release; Fa added, Fc changed, Fd deleted

formulas.name: Effort from productivity
formulas.formula: Effort = size / productivity; size = effort x rate

formulas.name: Project duration
formulas.formula: days = effort(person-hours) / (team size x hours per day)

formulas.name: Cost from effort
formulas.formula: cost = effort (PM) x monthly salary x team; or FP x productivity
formulas.note: Effort in person-months divided by team gives months

formulas.name: Software (Putnam) equation
formulas.note: Effort rises as fourth power of compression of time

formulas.name: Defect removal efficiency
formulas.note: E errors before delivery, D after

formulas.name: Cohesion ranking (best to worst)
formulas.formula: functional > sequential > communicational > procedural > temporal > logical > coincidental

formulas.name: Coupling ranking (low to high)
formulas.formula: data < stamp < control < external < common < content

formulas.name: Maintenance types
formulas.note: Restructuring appears as perfective in nov2020_q20

formulas.name: FDD order
formulas.formula: overall model, feature list, plan by feature, design by feature, build by feature

formulas.name: Coverage hierarchy
formulas.formula: path coverage implies branch implies statement coverage

formulas.name: ISO 9126 characteristics
formulas.formula: functionality, reliability, usability, efficiency, maintainability, portability
